title: Every save overwrites the whole notes list from one tab's memory, so a second open tab silently deletes the other tab's notes
evidence: app.js loads `notes` once (app.js:17-18) and never listens for the `storage` event or re-reads before writing. saveNotes writes the full in-memory array. Driven in Chromium: tab A and tab B open on the same origin; A created 'from A'; B (loaded before that) edited a body; localStorage 'notes' then held only ['first'].
failing_case: Open the app in two tabs. In tab A press New note and type a title; it shows 'Saved'. Switch to tab B (opened earlier) and type in any note. After 500 ms tab B writes its stale list. The note from tab A is gone from storage, with no error and no backup, and tab B still shows 'Saved'.
remediation: Before each write, re-read the stored list and merge by id (or write one key per note). Listen for the `storage` event and reload or merge the other tab's changes into `notes` and re-render.

title: Selecting or deleting a note by keyboard rebuilds the list and drops focus to <body>
evidence: renderList replaces every button on each call, including from selectNote and deleteNote (app.js:100, 121). Driven: focus the first .open button, press Enter; document.activeElement was BODY afterwards. Nothing restores focus to the clicked item or to the editor.
failing_case: A keyboard user tabs to a note in the list and presses Enter. Focus resets to the document start, so they must tab through the search box, New note and every list button again to reach the editor. After Delete, focus is also lost. Affects WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (A).
remediation: After rendering, restore focus: re-focus the button with the same data-id, or move focus to #title after opening a note and to the next item (or search box) after delete. Alternatively update rows in place instead of replacing them.

title: The field labelled 'Search notes' matches titles only; text in a note body is never found
evidence: Label at index.html:14 reads 'Search notes'. Driven: typed 'secretword' into a note body, waited for save, searched 'secretword': [redacted] list rows, and the message says 'No notes match' for text the user can see in a note.
failing_case: A user remembers a phrase from the body of a note and searches for it. The list shows 'No notes match "phrase"', which reads as if the note does not exist.
remediation: Also test n.body, or rename the label to 'Search titles' so it states what it does.
